# Extraction eval fixtures

Each `*.json` file in this directory is one fixture for `mileage/extraction_eval.py`:

```json
{
  "source_hint": "email:example_newsletter",
  "document": "<the raw document text/HTML the extractor sees>",
  "expected_rows": [
    {"program": "turkish", "region_a": "north_america", "region_b": "europe",
     "cabin": "business", "miles": 45000, "roundtrip": false}
  ]
}
```

`region_a`/`region_b` are canonical tokens (matching `charts.yaml::region_map`
values / `regions.canonicalize_region()` output), not raw prose, so scoring
doesn't depend on the extractor's own region-canonicalization choices lining
up with a human's prose reading of "Turkey" vs "Europe" — the eval is scoring
whether the extractor found the right *row*, using the same canonical
vocabulary every parser in this codebase already shares.

## IMPORTANT — all 26 fixtures here are synthetic, not real fixtures

They were hand-written (fixtures 01-04 as an initial bootstrap set, 05-26
generated by `_generate_bootstrap_set.py` to reach a broader synthetic
sample) to exercise the harness's plumbing AND to give the deterministic
extractor a real workout across messier phrasing — but they are NOT pulled
from real newsletters/blogs, and "20-30 synthetic fixtures" is not the same
deliverable as the plan's "20-30 real, hand-labeled" fixture set
(Cursor-Mileage-Plan.md §6.3). See `Cursor-LLM-Extractor-Task.md` at the repo
root for what real fixture collection should look like (pulling actual bodies
from `occulosequor@gmail.com` / creator blogs, then hand-correcting every
number) — that is still unstarted.

**What this synthetic set IS good for:** as of 2026-07-08 it gives a real,
measured baseline — `python -m mileage.extraction_eval` scores the
deterministic backend at **precision=0.68, recall=0.61, hallucinations=0**
across these 26 fixtures. Every miss/false-positive is annotated in its
fixture's `notes` field with the verified root cause (not a guess) — e.g.
cross-item bleed in bulleted multi-program roundups (`fixture_09`), a region
hint that appears before the number getting dropped when the program name is
mentioned after the number (`fixture_10`), the `program_zones`-style "within
X" fallback only being special-cased for `north_america` (`fixture_20` vs
`fixture_25`), and no temporal reasoning to discard a stale/historical price
sitting next to the current one (`fixture_26`). These are real, reproducible,
already-diagnosed gaps — exactly the kind of "cases the LLM should catch"
recall gap the plan describes, now with fixtures to prove it and a number
(0.61) to try to beat, rather than an assertion in a planning doc.

**Two fixtures (`fixture_15`, `fixture_22`, `fixture_23`) expect zero rows on
purpose** — pure devaluation chatter, a spelled-out number with no digit form
anywhere (which the grounding guard can *never* grip, by design — that's a
safety feature being tested, not a bug), and a routine booking-confirmation
email. Don't "fix" a future extractor to produce rows here.
